'''Lawrence Rocks''' (born August 27, 1933) is an American [[chemist]] and author who has written books on [[Energy crisis|energy crises]] and [[biofuel]]. He has also written about chemistry and [[sports]], specifically [[baseball]].

His 1973 book ''The Energy Crisis'' coincided with the [[1973 oil crisis]]. The book prompted public appearances and influenced the creation of the [[U.S. Department of Energy]].

Rocks' has also worked with professional baseball player [[Paul DeJong]] on the role of chemistry in baseball.

==Career==
Rocks received his Masters of Science degree from [[Purdue University]] and his [[Doctor of Science]] from [[Technische Hochschule Vienna]]. He wrote his doctoral thesis in [[Standard German|German]] in the field of [[analytical chemistry]] separating metal atoms in semi-aqueous solutions, which found that equilibrium constants are changed in semi-aqueous mediums.<ref>{{cite thesis |last= Rocks|first= Lawrence|date= 1964|title= Die Trennung von Mikromengen Calcium, Magnesium, Aluminium und Titan von grossen Mengen Eisen, Nickel und Chrom unter Anwendung von Pyrrolidindithiocarbamidat|type= D.Sc |publisher=Wien |oclc=637130820 }}</ref>

Rocks is Professor Emeritus of Chemistry at [[Long Island University]].<ref>Drellich, Evan. [http://blog.chron.com/ultimateastros/2014/08/20/a-professors-view-on-chemistry "A professor's view on chemistry, muscles, bones and injury"] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20141028044240/http://blog.chron.com/ultimateastros/2014/08/20/a-professors-view-on-chemistry |date=2014-10-28 }}, ' '[[Houston Chronicle]]' ', 20 August 2014. Retrieved on 20 August 2014.</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://newyork.cbslocal.com/video/3702658-body-chemistry-in-baseball/ |title=Body Chemistry in Baseball |date=2017-07-22 |access-date=2017-07-22}}</ref>

===Energy===

Rocks wrote ''The Energy Crisis'' (Crown, 1972). The book called for the formal establishment of a national energy center,<ref>{{cite book |last1=Rocks |first1=Lawrence |last2=Runyon |first2=Richard P |date=1972 |title=The Energy Crisis |publisher=Crown Publishers |isbn=978-0-517-501641 |url=https://archive.org/details/energycrisis00rock }}</ref> which influenced the creation of the [[U.S. Department of Energy]] by the Carter administration.<ref name=golden/>

Following publication, Rocks was discussed by ''[[Time Magazine]]''<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080603022707/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,907177,00.html] ' '[[Time Magazine]]' ' (May 7, 1973),</ref> and ''[[National Review]]''. He addressed the [[United Nations]], and appeared on ''[[The Today Show]]'', ''[[To Tell The Truth]]'',<ref>[http://www.ttttontheweb.com/tttt69s4guide.html#23], ' '[[To Tell The Truth]]' ', 1972-73 Episode Guide (' 'To Tell The Truth' ' version two, season four)</ref> and ''[[The Mike Douglas Show]]''.<ref>{{cite episode |title=[[The Mike Douglas Show]] |series=Season 12, Episode 87 |network=[[Broadcast syndication|syndicated]] |date=1 January 1974}}
[http://www.tv.com/shows/the-mike-douglas-show/january-1-1974-880504/] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190111033055/http://www.tv.com/shows/the-mike-douglas-show/january-1-1974-880504/ |date=2019-01-11 }}</ref> Rocks had a column in [[King Features Syndicate]].<ref name=golden>{{cite press release |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=A Golden Anniversary: Lawrence Rocks is First Faculty Member to Reach 50 Years of Service |url=http://www.liu.edu/~/media/Files/CWPost/About/NewsAndEvents/CampusNewsletters/PostPress/CWP_PostPress_Spring2009.ashx?la=en. |newspaper= Post Press |volume=18 |location= LIU.edu |issue= 1 |access-date= 18 December 2016 }}</ref>

After publication of ''The Energy Crisis'', Rocks authored the chemistry [[textbook]] ''Developing Your Chemistry Fundamentals'' (The Petroleum Publishing Company) in 1979.<ref>{{cite book|last=Rocks|first=Laurence|title=Developing Your Chemistry Fundamentals|date=1979 |publisher=PPC Books |isbn = 978-0878140411}}</ref>

In 1980 Rocks authored ''Fuels For Tomorrow'' (PennWell Publishers 1980), a sequel to ''The Energy Crisis'', in which Rocks stated that the future of agriculture will be in [[Industrial fermentation|fermentation chemistry]], a process he asserted was far less hazardous to the environment.<ref>{{cite book|last=Rocks |first=Lawrence|title=Fuels for Tomorrow: Lawrence Rocks: 9780878141357|year=1980|publisher=PennWell Book |isbn = 978-0878141357}}</ref>

===Sports===

In 2017 Rocks conducted an experiment studying the effect temperature has on a baseball, with [[Paul DeJong]] as his laboratory assistant. The outcome of the experiment was that the optimal bounce of a baseball lies between 68-75 degrees Fahrenheit because at lower temperatures the elastomeres become more rigid and become softer at higher temperatures.<ref name=cardinals>{{Cite AV media|access-date=November 9, 2017|title=Cardinals' DeJong, Renowned Scientist Test Effects Of Heat On Baseball|url=http://newyork.cbslocal.com/tag/dr-lawrence-rocks/|publisher=CBS New York}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://headlines.liu.edu/?p=1012 |title= LIU Post Scientist Teams Up with Cardinals' DeJong |date=2017-11-10 |access-date=2017-11-10}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://stlouis.cbslocal.com/2017/12/13/cardinals-dejong-shortstop-position-epiphany-rookie/ |title= DeJong's 'Epiphany' Came After A Full-Time Move To Shortstop |date=2017-12-13 |access-date=2017-12-13}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pjstar.com/sports/20180112/paul-dejong-shares-his-story-his-time-at-cardinals-caravan|title=Paul DeJong shares his story, his time at Cardinals Caravan |first=Dave|last=Allen |publisher=Journal Star|access-date=January 12, 2018}}</ref>

While appearing on [[MLB Network]] during the 2017 winter meetings, Rocks defined sports chemistry as "the combination of modern analytical chemistry with sports metrics."<ref>{{Cite AV media|access-date=December 12, 2017|title=MLB Now: DeJong and Dr. Rocks|url=https://www.mlb.com/video/mlb-now-dejong-and-dr-rocks/c-1869854783|publisher=MLB.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://headlines.liu.edu/?p=1088|title= LIU Post Scientist Featured on MLB Network |date= 15 December 2017 |publisher=Long Island University |access-date=December 15, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media|access-date=December 12, 2017|title=Sports chemistry in baseball |url=https://www.mlb.com/phillies/video/sports-chemistry-in-baseball/c-1869849783?tid=49502780|publisher=MLB.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mlb.com/news/holiday-qa-with-cardinals-paul-dejong/c-263710992|title=Q&A: DeJong talks offseason, holidays & more |first=Jenifer|last=Langosch |work=MLB.com|access-date=December 22, 2017}}</ref> In 2018

==Personal life==
He and his wife Marlene have one son, [[Burton Rocks]], who is a writer and sports agent.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stltoday.com/sports/baseball/professional/cards-notebook-dejong-visits-meetings-talking-chemistry/article_fccb01f3-0b8b-5b02-b6f1-31b254264c27.html|title=Cards' DeJong talks chemistry (not the clubhouse kind) at winter meetings |first=Derrick|last=Goold |date=13 December 2017 |publisher=St. Louis Post-Dispatch|access-date=December 13, 2017}}</ref> He is a supporter of the Palm Beach Symphony.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://shinyshots.palmbeachdailynews.com/mycapture/folder.asp?event=2187847&CategoryID=48024&ListSubAlbums=0|title=Palm Beach Symphony 16th ANNUAL GALA at The Breakers|work=Palm Beach Daily News|access-date=February 21, 2018|archive-date=February 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180223051555/http://shinyshots.palmbeachdailynews.com/mycapture/folder.asp?event=2187847&CategoryID=48024&ListSubAlbums=0|url-status=dead}}</ref>
